findings.description: Direct inspection of all five current V12 views and six pose renders shows the plain ivory jacket, broad lavender diagonal panel and oversized elbow diamonds are still simplistic and do not yet read as a finished fencing-practice outfit; rear and side garment detailing remains sparse.

The 60 mm longer hem and restrained wrap reduce the standing flare slightly, but the overskirt remains a broad shell. Cosine pleat displacement on the current coarse panel mesh still renders as angular, jagged folds rather than controlled sewn pleats.

Current geometric overskirt ray coverage of upper-thigh samples is neutral L/R 0.5243/0.5232, crouch 0.3887/0.3853, and sit 0.3299/0.3299. Coverage improved over V11 but shorts remain visibly exposed during crouch and sit. These geometry diagnostics do not grant fit acceptance.

Crouch and seated views still show the skirt lifting and breaking into rigid angular folds; prone view forms a wide uneven fan. The moderate length increase and smooth radial fold field did not resolve deformation or pose coverage.
Arms-up and arm-cross views retain faceted sleeve/underarm surfaces, and the elbow diamonds still read as oversized surface decals rather than restrained quilted patches.
Back and profile renders remain plain and faceted, with no convincing finished rear-waist adjustment or clean panel transition.

sourceEvidence.currentPrototypeMotif: V12 tests a 60 mm hem continuation, restrained panel flare, and cosine pleat seed. Direct review confirms improved standing thigh coverage, but visible pose exposure, jagged angular folds, sparse styling, and faceted surfaces remain below acceptance.

nextAction: REJECT; do not repeat the cosine displacement on the current coarse shell. Change the skirt mesh method to add longitudinal/radial subdivisions with a controlled sewn pleat profile, directly address crouch/sit/prone shorts exposure, and refine jacket/back/elbow details before another prototype review.
